added_failures_note: the reviewed manifest leaves baseline_suite null, so the pair was read from the run's own arms: base-arm head-tests.log runs tests/test_picker.py at base b5060830 (9 failed, 18 passed, EXIT=1) and the after arm verified-head-tests.log reports 32 passed at 6d24a423 (EXIT=0); the review re-ran the after arm at the reviewed head 486058680 and got 32 passed EXIT=0. The head therefore adds no failure the base did not already carry - zero added failures.

findings.text: follow-on: the replay summary's median_jev_latency_ms takes statistics.median over all 50 rows' jev_latency_ms, but the ~29 deterministic exact-local-rule rows carry jev_latency_ms 0.0 and no Jev call, so the summary reports 0.0 (replay.json summary) while the actual median across the 21 Jev calls is 350.278 ms (replay-audit.json, and the fragment's headline figure); a reader taking the summary's jev latency is given a value that measures the rule rows, not the calls.

follow-on: the replay summary's refused_model_picks counts rows whose selected backend is codex-spark or whose model is gated by REFUSED_BACKENDS/REFUSED_MODELS before the picker runs, so it is structurally zero and cannot fail; the headline 'refused-model picks 0' is therefore guaranteed by construction rather than measured - the guard that can actually fire is the mutation-verified test_refused_model_is_never_offered_to_jev and its recorded negative control.

follow-on: test_representative_state_is_bounded_and_comment_verbatim builds its candidates with _lane stubbed to return congestion {'waiting': 0}, so the rendered representative state (and the published 593-token figure in state-size.json) carries one congestion key where a real local lane reading carries five (live-selection.json shows running, waiting, admission_verdict, stale, slots_state); the 1,500-token bound is measured against a smaller state than production renders, so the bound understates the real shape it is meant to cap.

item_verdicts.goal: the node builds reckon/crew/picker/ (strict Jinja loader, state and question templates, candidate adapter, typed Jev client, typed selection, replay) and a 'reckon crew pick' command that prints one selection and dispatches nothing; reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:47 pick, picker/snapshot.py:137 candidates and picker/replay.py:17 replay are those, and the design note in the fragment names every question, the state schema with the orchestrator-comment field, the candidate filter, both confidence thresholds, the fallback, the pinned Jev version and the credential path, with a 50-row replay.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 8f0025cee..486058680, negative control recorded, after_suite populated at 6d24a423; baseline_suite is null so the added-failure pair was read from the run's own base-arm log (head-tests.log) and after arm (verified-head-tests.log).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares reckon/crew/picker, reckon/cli.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, tests/test_picker.py, the picker-prototype fragment and a figures dir; the five commits touch exactly those source and test paths plus the fragment and pyproject/uv.lock, every one inside the declared scope and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/test_picker.py covers the refusals, both threshold boundaries, exact-local routing with Jev asserted not called, strict missing-fact raising, malformed/NaN answers, unreachable Jev, verbatim comment round-trip, the state bound, credential loading, outcomes filtering and replay ordering under mocked Jev; the declared mutation reddens test_refused_model_is_never_offered_to_jev at the refused-model assertion; the deductions are the two replay summary metrics that no test can redden and the bound test's stubbed one-key congestion.
justifications.evidence: the after arm reproduces at the reviewed head - tests/test_picker.py 32 passed at 486058680 (verified-head-tests.log, and independently re-run here at EXIT=0) - and the account-refused guard reproduces red under the declared mutation (negative-control-head.log, reproduced here in a scratch tree at EXIT=1 on the exact assertion); the deductions are the replay summary's median_jev_latency_ms, which reports 0.0 against the 350.278 ms the fragment quotes, and the structurally-zero refused_model_picks headline.
justifications.fit: the package follows the repo's stdlib-and-dataclass style, ruff check adds no finding (lint-delta.json shows head == base), uv lock --check passes, it reuses the existing budget/context/competence/serving/lane gates rather than reimplementing them, and no symbol carries a plan label; the one deduction is that the evidence fragment carries tables but no figure, where a candidate-filter diagram would meet the graphics mandate for a design note.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the prototype delivers exactly what §5's first node and §4's done-when ask: a strict-Jinja picker package, the 'reckon crew pick' command with no dispatch, and a 50-row replay; the design note documents the question, state schema, candidate filter, 0.6/0.4 thresholds, fallback, pinned typesafe/jev-1.13 and the credential path; the only deduction is that §4's 'compare with a single Choice over every (family, model) pair' is addressed implicitly (a backend name is one family/model pair) rather than argued as the fragment does for the rejected two-question design.
justifications.scope_discipline: the five commits touch only the declared paths - reckon/crew/picker/*, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_picker.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock and the picker-prototype fragment - with no edit to any shared plan, index or dispatch path; plan_dispatch and the live ledger are untouched.
